subject: GPU run-rate deficit & reserved throughput shortfall — urgent exec/procurement briefing
messages:
From: Sandeep Reddy <sandeep@bluefinpay.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@bluefinpay.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden latency & 500s impacting checkout (Dedicated pool / reserved shortfall)

Priya —

Quick heads up from our SRE team: starting ~08:45 PT we’ve seen a steady rise in 95p latency for inference calls backed by our dedicated GPU pool (model pinned to gpt-redwood-4b-dedicated). Concurrently error rate (500/502) climbed to ~6% and tail latency pushed timeouts on our checkout path. We’re on a tight transaction window — this is blocking several merchants.

Attached: short window latency graph and a sample of error traces. We were previously hitting the reserved throughput we purchased; current metrics show a run-rate below the committed reservation (tokens/sec), causing queued requests and timeouts.

Can Redwood:
- Confirm whether this is capacity starvation on the dedicated pool vs a kernel/runtime degradation?
- Authorize immediate temporary burst capacity or fallback to hosted variants while we stabilize?

We need an exec-visible response and a plan within the hour — ops is monitoring.

— Sandeep
BlueFin Payments, Head of Platform / SRE
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Sandeep Reddy <sandeep@bluefinpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & 500s impacting checkout (Dedicated pool / reserved shortfall)

Sandeep —

Thanks for the alert and the attachments. We’re pulling telemetry now. Quick answers up-front: 1) we see your headroom has depleted on the reserved pool (tokens/sec below contract line) and there’s a small cluster-level imbalance causing queueing; 2) there are no active kernel regressions flagged yet but we’re validating.

Immediate actions I’m initiating now:
- Ops (marissa) to open a priority bridge with Prod Infra and throttle non-essential tenants on the same pool.
- Commercial (rishi) to work on immediate burst credit authorization and confirm procurement path for temporary capacity.
- Naomi (account lead) to draft a concise MAP and exec note for BlueFin leadership.

Request for you: can you attach a 30s token histogram and a single failing request payload (redact PII) so infra can reproduce?

I’ll escalate to our Head of Ops and CFO for temporary capacity sign-off if infra confirms we need burst GPUs. I’ll post an executive summary and the bridge link in 20 minutes.

-priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Sandeep Reddy <sandeep@bluefinpay.com>, ops@bluefinpay.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & 500s impacting checkout (Dedicated pool / reserved shortfall)

Bridge up: https://bridges.redwood.ai/room/bluefin-urgent-20250618
Attendees: Prod Infra, Runtime, Customer SRE (BlueFin).

Findings so far (first pass):
- Dedicated pool (dp-34) shows sustained CUDA queue depth spike at 08:42 — sustained for ~35m.
- KV-cache pressure on the model shard that BlueFin uses — cache misses increased 4x vs baseline, increasing per-request compute (longer context rebuilds).
- Running processes show one tenant with a misconfigured batch multiplier that expired autoscaling headroom earlier than expected (0400-0800 overnight increase). We’ve isolated the tenant and set a temporary limit.

Proposed immediate mitigation (3 steps):
1) Apply temporary cap on noisy tenant and re-balance shards (infra action) — ETA 12m.
2) Enable cross-pool fallback: route new BlueFin requests to a compatible hosted variant for latency-sensitive endpoints (config safety checks completed) — ETA 18m; requires procurement/burst approval for incremental cost.
3) Apply short-lived prefix caching for high-frequency checkout prompt patterns to cut token extraction overhead — ETA 30m.

Marissa (infra) will update the bridge with logs and a condensed runbook. If we confirm cross-pool fallback we’ll need commercial authorization for the next 24–48 hours of hosted run. Rishi, can you confirm how fast we can sign a short-term supplement and the channel for approval?

—Marissa
Director, Production Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Sandeep Reddy <sandeep@bluefinpay.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 14:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & 500s impacting checkout (Dedicated pool / reserved shortfall)

Update and commercial path:

We’ve provisionally authorized 48 hours of burst capacity on hosted variants pending a rapid amendment to the DF-9812 SOW (attachment: requested-MAP-draft.pdf). Procurement can sign on an emergency addendum with a PO or credit card; Legal has routed a one-page amendment to DocuSign — link posted in the bridge.

Cost estimate (ballpark): additional $7k–$12k/day depending on model flavor and QPS. We’ll absorb the first 6 hours via an emergency credit (exec discretionary) while BlueFin evaluates longer coverage.

Next steps for BlueFin:
- Accept temporary routing to hosted variant for checkout endpoints (ops will provide the exact endpoint and rollout window).
- Provide the token histogram + sample failing payload that Priya requested; that helps infra validate the KV-cache mitigation.

Naomi will prepare an exec summary for the CTO/CEO readout; I’ll coordinate the emergency SOW amendment with Procurement and Legal.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
